SIMY, told through a comic

Take the doctor’s words and work through them in practice.
Take that preparation into the real conversation.

Fictional characters, doctor roles and dialogue illustrate a proposed use. Real meeting records are kept distinct from AI roleplay. Recording permissions and integration details are reviewed during implementation.

01 / Hear the doctor’s concerns

MRDoctor: “I’d like to check the basis of that comparison.”
Bring those words into the next preparation.

Record the real meeting with the required consent and in line with company and facility rules. Preserve the doctor’s words alongside the surrounding conversation.

02 / Identify interests and follow-up questions

SIMYWhat the doctor wants to check is whether the study population reflects their own practice. Is that right?

Organize statements, concerns and follow-up questions from recordings and transcripts. The MR checks the interpretation against the original conversation.

03 / Rehearse the questions for the next meeting

SIMYBuilding on the previous follow-up question,
practice asking which comparison conditions matter.

Combine public information and approved materials with what the real meeting revealed. Set questions and responses around that doctor’s interests and the next meeting’s purpose.

04 / Try saying it out loud

MRMR: “I’ve brought the comparison materials.”
AI doctor: “Before that, which patient population are we discussing?”

The explanation began before the doctor’s question was clarified. Practice helps reveal where the conversation went off track.

05 / Change the question and try again

MR“Which differences in patient characteristics concern you?”
This time, start with what the doctor wants to clarify.

Try again with the same doctor role. Review the relevant statements and refine the order of questions and how evidence is explained.

06 / Use the rehearsed question in the next meeting

MRMR: “Which differences in patient characteristics concern you?”
Doctor: “I want to clarify the differences in prior treatment. Next, I’d also like to discuss responsibilities in the hospital.”
The rehearsed question helped me ask which conditions the doctor wanted to clarify.

Try the revised way of asking in the real meeting. Record the doctor’s response and new follow-up questions with consent and in line with company rules, then use them to prepare for the next visit.

07 / New conversations update the practice

SIMYNext, alongside the comparison,
practice clarifying roles within the hospital.

Reflect new statements and follow-up questions in the next practice. Keep personalizing as conversations evolve, rather than treating the doctor’s interests as fixed.

08 / Turn individual reflection into team development

Branch manager / Training teamWho needs support, and in which situations?
Let’s use that insight in the next training.

Identify practice trends and challenges within agreed sharing permissions. The proposed approach supports individual coaching and improvements to training materials.

PREPARE, PRACTICE, PUT INTO ACTION

Turn insights and practice
into action at the next meeting.

Review the doctor’s interests and the conditions they want to clarify from the last meeting. Rehearse how to ask and explain, then use that preparation in the next real conversation. Reflect on the doctor’s response to prepare for the following visit.

  1. Record and transcribe the meeting
  2. Review statements and follow-up questions
  3. Rehearse for the next meeting
  4. Use the rehearsed questions in the meeting
  5. Use the doctor’s response to prepare the next visit
What to learn from the meeting

What does the doctor want to clarify?

  • Topics of interest and repeated questions
  • Conditions that matter in decisions, such as comparison or safety management
  • Questions the previous explanation did not resolve
  • Items promised for confirmation before the next meeting
What to put into action at the next meeting

What should you ask this doctor, and how?

  • The opening question for the meeting
  • How to adjust questions and explanations to the doctor’s response
  • Evidence, conditions and limitations to check in approved materials
  • Answers to the previous follow-up questions and points still to clarify

Follow company and healthcare facility rules and obtain the required consent before recording. Agree in advance on information use, storage and viewing permissions, and handle patient personal information under internal policies. The responsible person checks AI summaries and inferences against original statements. Safety information, including adverse events, must be promptly escalated through designated reporting channels.

START WITH YOUR MATERIALS

Before recording begins,
start with existing materials.

Start with approved materials or internal roleplay recordings while recording procedures are being established. Once real meeting records can be used, add the doctor’s statements and follow-up questions to deepen personalization. Scenario design support for existing AI roleplay tools can also be explored.

Useful starting materials

Build on what is ready.

  • Approved training materials and sample answers
  • Defined doctor profiles and expected questions
  • Internal roleplay recordings and transcripts
  • Learning objectives and evaluation criteria
What we define together

Start with one situation, test and refine.

  • The doctor role and purpose of the practice
  • Responses and conversation paths
  • Statements to evaluate and points for reflection
  • Review by the responsible team and improvements after trials

Confirm rights to use materials and how confidential information is handled. Support for existing tools depends on their input formats and usage constraints. The responsible team selects repeatable questions and ways of checking understanding from strong internal examples for use in training.

01 / PERSONALIZED ROLEPLAY

Different doctors.
Different questions and responses.

Combine public information and training materials with statements, interests and follow-up questions confirmed from real meeting recordings. Shape questions and responses around each doctor’s decision criteria and the purpose of the next meeting.

Doctor A / Scrutinizes evidence

“Which patient population are we discussing?”

The last follow-up concerned the basis of a comparison. Practice with a doctor role that probes the limitations after evidence is presented.

MR: “Following up on the comparison, which patient profiles would you like to clarify?”
AI doctor: “Whether prior treatment and the study population overlap with my practice.”
Practice focus: ask which conditions need clarification.
Doctor B / Cautious about safety management

“Who checks what?”

The last follow-up concerned roles within the hospital. Move from implementation procedures to explanations for families.

MR: “Following up on safety management, which responsibilities still need clarification?”
AI doctor: “We need to define what the clinical team and those explaining to patients each handle.”
Practice focus: ask about specific concerns.

Doctor settings and dialogue are fictional. Distinguish sources from assumptions, and never treat AI roleplay as a record of a real meeting. Check product explanations against the latest approved materials.

Build training around four MR and two MSL scenarios.

MR / Explore the doctor’s decision criteria
  • Product A: a busy, practical doctor
  • Product B: a doctor who scrutinizes evidence
  • Product C: a doctor cautious about explanations for families
  • Product D: a doctor strict about safety management
MSL / Non-promotional scientific dialogue
  • Product A: a doctor who scrutinizes research methods
  • Product B: a doctor open to research collaboration

Clarify the population, limitations of evidence and unresolved questions. Sales and prescribing gains are not evaluation criteria.

Products A–D are practice examples. Agree on priority areas, approved materials and evaluation criteria, with separate objectives and assessments for MR and MSL activities.

02 / MEETING QUALITY

Bring explanation quality
into the next meeting.

SQM identifies items to review from recordings and transcripts of real meetings. The responsible team checks the surrounding explanation and source materials. The proposed use is to rehearse an improved explanation with the same doctor role and apply it in the next meeting.

Fictional conversation and proposed use. Accuracy and integration for real meetings are unverified. AI suggests items for review; the supervising team makes the final decision. Safety information is escalated separately and promptly.

03 / TEAM DEVELOPMENT

From individual practice
to team development.

We propose a setup that brings together participation, strengths, challenges and repeat practice across branches and the company. Managers can identify where support is needed and use insights for priority training and individual coaching.

  2. Branch overview
  3. Company overview
